title: Inspect an installed in-service brake rotor's thickness with an outside micrometer
instruction: Inspect the installed in-service brake rotor: measure its thickness at the marked point on the wear band with the outside micrometer, and leave the micrometer on its rest showing the reading.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, ~0.7 million US jobs, BLS OEWS approximate) check brake rotor thickness at every brake job: the wheel is removed, the caliper unbolted (its bracket stays on the knuckle), the worn disc cleaned, and thickness measured with a 0-25 mm outside micrometer at eight points around the friction band, comparing the smallest reading with the discard thickness stamped on the rotor (19 mm here). The standard technique holds the frame square on the band and rocks it slightly to find the true minimum while the other hand turns the ratchet stop until it clicks (5-10 N measuring force).
setup: Left and right are the robot's; positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the table. A worn, in-service front brake rotor (Brembo 09.7012.11: 280 mm diameter, 22.0 mm new, 19 mm discard, 65 mm centre bore, 5 x 100 mm stud holes, grey cast iron; ~5.74 kg worn mass estimated from 0.25 mm wear per face) is bolted to its front hub and steering knuckle in an installed wheel well, its axis along y at z 0.152 m, centre x 0.508, y ~0.1208. Eight 2 mm scribe marks at radius 135 mm (5 mm inboard of the 140 mm friction rim) show the real inspection points; a 6 mm paint dot at 135 mm radius, 10 degrees above the 9 o'clock line (facing the robot), marks the thinnest point and the scored spot. Fixed installed context: a cast-iron hub flange (110 mm dia x 12 mm), bearing housing (90 mm dia x 40 mm), upright (~180 mm tall), lower ball-joint boss, strut clamp, steering arm and five M12 wheel studs on the 100 mm circle; a painted-steel caliper carrier bracket at 6 o'clock with a bridge over the disc rim and two ears bolted to the knuckle. The caliper and pads are removed for the inspection, leaving the friction band open; none of this hardware moves. A 0-25 mm outside micrometer of the Mitutoyo 103-137 class (free: 175 g, 18 mm thimble, 6.35 mm faces, 0.5 mm pitch, ratchet stop, lock lever, spindle fully open at 25.0 mm) lies across the two 46 x 6 x 146 mm uprights of a 6061-T6 aluminium rest (80 x 80 x 30 mm base, 36 mm clear gap, 0.8 mm EPDM caps) at x 0.330, y 0.165, its axis along y, its throat toward +x. A real trial scans the eight points to find the thinnest, then measures the reference there (README).
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand at the end. (1) The micrometer was closed square on the worn rotor's friction band at the marked spot: its anvil face centre 100 to 136 mm from the hub axis and within 5 mm of the dot, the anvil on the rotor's face (within 1 mm), its axis within 5 degrees of the hub axis, and the reading within +-0.02 mm of the rotor's measured thickness at the dot (21.50 mm in the sim; the worn part's actual value measured at the thinnest of eight inspection points per real trial, README; +-0.05 mm only with a 0.01 mm-grade reference). (2) With step 1, the ratchet clicked (slipped a tooth) at least twice with the faces on the rotor. (3) With step 2, the micrometer is off the rotor and its reading is within +-0.02 mm of that measured thickness. (4) With step 3, the micrometer lies on its rest (within 12 mm, 4 mm up, 6 degrees), no gripper holds it and no pad is within 3 cm. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four have held together for 1 s with the micrometer within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8. Scoring 0 for the whole run: the micrometer falling off the table, or dropped (falling faster than 0.6 m/s with nothing holding it).
reset_notes: The wheel stays installed: rotor on the hub, five stud nuts and the caliper bracket on the knuckle, the caliper and pads off, the eight marks and the paint dot in place. For a new trial, clean the wear band with isopropyl alcohol and let it dry. Lay the micrometer across the rest's ribs with the spindle fully open (25.0 mm), the lock lever unlocked and the ratchet at rest; nothing is held. If the paint dot has rubbed off, re-scan the eight points at radius 135 mm and re-mark the thinnest with a 6 mm dot before the trial (README).
fidelity: Declared: the worn rotor is the real Brembo part (280 mm dia, 22.0 mm new, 19 mm discard), 21.50 mm in the sim; the hub, knuckle and caliper bracket are fixed installed context at representative (estimated) sizes. The thread (0.5 mm/turn), ratchet (0.006 N m slip, 18-deg clicks), 6 N measuring force (drive capped at 10 N) and frame/lever dimensions are estimates. The +-0.02 mm band needs a 0.001 mm reference (+-0.05 mm with 0.01 mm). Measurement physics is unchanged from the bench version.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (re-run on the revised scene, 3,200-step limit). Demo: 1.0 at step 2815 on MuJoCo (kept 21.516 mm, +0.016) and 1.0 on Isaac (kept 21.518 mm, +0.018; success near step 2825). pytest 40.
